newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May consumer prices up 0.75 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May consumer prices up 0.75 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's May consumer price index rose 0.75 percent compared to May 1996, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Thursday.
The May wholesale price index was down 1.89 percent compared to a year earlier, the directorate said.
The May consumer price index rise was well below an average forecast for a rise of 1.33 percent that resulted from a June 3 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
Consumer prices grew just 0.1 percent compared to April, when annual CPI growth had come in at just 0.50 percent, according to a revision issued on Thursday by the directorate.

Government economists attributed the low month-on-month rise to stabilisation of retail pork prices, which had plummeted in March and April due to an islandwide outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease. The epidemic had slashed pork consumption.
What little rise there was in May consumer prices was attributed primarily to a slight increase in medical costs, the directorate said.
The minor year-on-year consumer price increase reflected a relatively low rise in prices of agricultural products.
May's wholesale price index rose 0.73 percent compared with April, when annual WPI growth registered a negative 2.67 percent growth.
The month-on-month WPI rise was due to a recovery of wholesale hog prices, the directorate said.
"Wholesale hog prices have recovered to the level prior to the the outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease," directorate director Chan Teh-song told a news conference.
Consumer prices rose by an average of only 1.27 percent year-on-year between January and May, making 1997 inflation to date the lowest on record since 1989, Chan said.
He said the directorate maintained a forecast for 1997 CPI growth at 2.01 percent.
